relation_specs.label: PRECONDITION
relation_specs.direction: source event establishes, enables, motivates, or is required for the target event
relation_specs.definition: A directed event-event relation where the source is a prerequisite, enabling condition, motivating circumstance, or necessary setup for the target.
relation_specs.negative_note: Do not choose merely because the source is mentioned earlier. Semantic dependency is required.

relation_specs.label: FALLING_ACTION
relation_specs.direction: source event is connected to a downstream, follow-up, consequence, continuation, aftermath, or elaborating event represented by the target
relation_specs.definition: A directed storyline relation linking an event to a subsequent/downstream consequence, continuation, aftermath, or narratively dependent event when PRECONDITION is not the better interpretation.
relation_specs.negative_note: Do not invert the pair and do not use this as a generic co-occurrence label.

layer01.goal: Extract a high-recall exact event inventory with parallel sentence passes and whole-document coverage reviews, then generate directed EventStoryLine PLOT_LINK candidates from a closed inventory in complete source batches.
event_mentions: Extract explicit eventive verbs, participles, infinitival events, complete phrasal verbs, eventive nouns and nominalizations, processes, occurrences, and explicit states/conditions.
Process every story sentence independently, then perform whole-document coverage reviews for missed nominals, states, embedded predicates, and repeated mentions.
Represent each mention as S{sentence}[start:end]::trigger using zero-based end-exclusive source-token offsets.
Keep repeated lexical triggers as distinct mentions whenever their indexed spans differ.
Preserve complete phrasal verbs, multi-token expressions, and every tokenized component of hyphenated triggers.
Reject people, organizations, locations, dates, objects, URLs, publication metadata, connective-only spans, auxiliary-only spans, and inferred events not explicitly evoked.
Do not use a gold event lexicon, gold event count, gold spans, or gold relation pairs.
relations: Generate candidate PLOT_LINK pairs only after the event inventory is validated and closed.
Cover every source event through bounded parallel source batches; endpoints must reference closed-inventory IDs.

Treat PLOT_LINK as broader than strict causality: setup, enabling context, motivation, consequence, continuation, aftermath, follow-up, elaboration, and headline/body narrative development may qualify.
Include supported cross-sentence and repeated-mention links, while rejecting mere co-occurrence or sentence order alone.
Use a lexical relation cue rather than PRECONDITION or FALLING_ACTION; Layer 2 selects the canonical relation.
Preserve source-to-target direction and never invent, alter, or swap event spans.

phases.phase_a1: Parallel sentence-level exhaustive event inventory extraction.
phases.phase_a2: Two whole-document missing-event reviews over the validated union.
phases.phase_b: Parallel source-batched PLOT_LINK proposal generation over the closed event inventory.

layer02.goal: Choose exactly PRECONDITION or FALLING_ACTION for one already extracted event pair, or found=false.
rules: EventStoryLine PLOT_LINK is broader than strict physical causality; use narrative dependency supported by the document.
PRECONDITION is preferred when the source is rising-action context that enables, motivates, requires, prepares, or sets up the target.
FALLING_ACTION is preferred when the target is a consequence, continuation, aftermath, follow-up, elaboration, or downstream narrative development.
Cross-sentence and repeated-mention links are allowed when semantically supported.
Choose found=false for mere topical co-occurrence, unsupported direction, or a pair lacking narrative dependency.

layer04.goal: Resolve exact event keys to their native event candidates and preserve the Layer 2 direction.
rules: Both endpoints must be event candidates.
Never swap source and target to improve apparent plausibility.
Reject a relation when either indexed event key cannot be resolved uniquely.

synthetic_relation_examples.text: The court order required the defendant to enter treatment.
synthetic_relation_examples.explanation: The order establishes a required condition for entering treatment.

synthetic_relation_examples.text: The collision was followed by an investigation.
synthetic_relation_examples.explanation: The investigation is a downstream follow-up to the collision.

synthetic_relation_examples.text: Hiring counsel enabled the appeal to proceed.
synthetic_relation_examples.explanation: The first event enables the second.

synthetic_relation_examples.text: The announcement triggered protests, followed by arrests.
synthetic_relation_examples.explanation: The arrests are part of the downstream storyline after the announcement.

negative_examples.text: S2[4:5]::meeting and S5[9:10]::speech occur in the same article
negative_examples.explanation: Co-occurrence alone is not a relation.
A person is not an event endpoint.
A date is not an event endpoint.
The dataset's null key is excluded from the relation vocabulary and evaluation.

seed_ontology_role: Temporal grounding only; PRECONDITION and FALLING_ACTION remain the controlled normalized benchmark relation labels.
evaluation_scope: All 443 normalized EventStoryLine records (type full + test); null pairs excluded.

event_span_examples.rule: Keep the phrasal-verb particle inside the event trigger.
Keep every tokenized component of a hyphenated event trigger.
A multi-token state/event expression may begin with a function word when the complete span is eventive.

development_note: The one-document document is used for profile development. Freeze this v1.3 profile before the five-document smoke and full 443-document evaluation.
